Mercedes T-Bones Two CLAs in World's First Public High-Speed Side Impact Crash Test
40 photos
Photo: Mercedes-Benz on YouTube / edited
Mercedes-Benz AG crashed a hybrid CLA Shooting Brake into the driver's side of an electric CLA Sedan to demonstrate how safe the new compact models are in a real-world crash scenario. The high-voltage battery of the EV survived just fine, the hybrid shut down its fuel system as intended, and most importantly, both safety cells preserved their occupant space.
According to the Stuttgart-based automaker, every crash test dummy stayed below the relevant injury assessment limits. While a frontal crash gives Mercedes engineers the length of the nose and its crumple zones to work with, a side impact brings the impact much closer to the people inside the vehicle.
There is less structure available to deform before the passenger compartment takes the load. In the electric CLA Sedan, the target also included the edge of the underfloor high-voltage battery. With this 35-mph (56-kph) test, Mercedes chose a collision scenario that asks the vehicle's unibody construction to protect both the occupants and the battery at once.
Said cars met at 90 degrees, with each weighing more than 2,000 kilograms (4,409 pounds) as equipped. That's a lot for a compact, but hey, even compacts are hideously heavy in this day and age. The hybrid CLA Shooting Brake hit the other with its front structure, traveling at the very same 35 miles per hour as the electric CLA Sedan.
Mercedes deliberately ran the test without AEB, as it normally does for this kind of assessment, because Mercedes wanted to examine how the structure and restraints deal with the impact conditions. Eight dummies were tested in total, representing four adults and four children, totaling up to 150 measurement points apiece.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz on YouTube All their readings are reported to have remained below the applicable biomechanical thresholds, indicating a low risk of serious injury. Even so, bear in mind this is a manufacturer-performed test rather than Euro NCAP or the IIHS working their magic with no interest at all in defending a manufacturer's product.
Crash footage published by Merc on YouTube shows how the crumple zones absorb energy while the safety belts, their pretensioners, and the airbags manage the occupants' movement during the impact. As if the undamaged traction battery wasn't good enough of a result, the zero-emission CLA Sedan also shut down its high-voltage system automatically, disconnecting the battery from the drivetrain.
The gas-drinking CLA Shooting Brake, which features an electrified dual-clutch transmission boasting a third clutch on the input shaft that completely disconnects the 1.5-liter gasser from the drivetrain for improved fuel economy, took a different post-crash precaution by cutting off its fuel system. This way, the hybridized model reduces the risk of a vehicle fire in the event of a serious impact.
Both CLAs further unlocked their doors, partly lowered the side windows, and triggered an eCall automatic emergency call. Mercedes calls this a world first, namely the first public high-speed side impact crash test. By comparison, the IIHS side impact crash test uses a deformable barrier striking rig that hits the driver's side at 37 mph (60 kph) while the vehicle remains completely stationary.
Euro NCAP uses two distinct side impact tests to evaluate how a vehicle protects its occupants. The side mobile barrier test is conducted at 60 kph (37 mph) as opposed to 32 kph (20 mph) for the side pole test. The car is stationary in the mobile barrier test. Having cleared that up, Merc's T-bone test is the real deal in terms of impact forces.

source_document.body:
Tesla reports its third-quarter 2026 financial results tomorrow, October 21, after the market closes. The earnings call follows at 5:30 p.m. ET.
Wall Street expects revenue to come in flat and earnings per share to drop 10% from a year ago, even though Tesla just beat its own delivery consensus by more than 24,000 vehicles.
Tesla Q3 2026 deliveries and energy deployment
We already have the volume numbers. Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in Q3 , down 2.1% from its all-time record of 497,099 in Q3 2025, but well above the 461,974 consensus Tesla compiled from 24 analysts.
It built only 464,391 vehicles during the quarter. So Tesla delivered 22,141 more cars than it produced, the second quarter in a row it has worked down inventory after building roughly 50,000 excess vehicles in Q1.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
It’s still a two-car company. Model 3 and Model Y made up 478,237 of those deliveries, while “other models” (Cybertruck, Semi and what’s left of Model S and X) fell 48% year-over-year to 8,295 units.
Energy storage was the weak spot. Tesla deployed 13.7 GWh, up 9.6% from 12.5 GWh a year ago, but well short of the roughly 15.9 GWh analysts expected and below the 14.2 GWh record it set in Q4 2025.
Tesla Q3 2026 revenue
The Wall Street consensus calls for $28.06 billion in revenue, with the Estimize crowd a bit more bullish at $28.36 billion. Either way, that’s flat against the $28.1 billion Tesla reported in Q3 2025. Wall Street estimates range from $25.1 billion to $30.6 billion.
Wall Street and Estimize consensus for Tesla’s Q3 2026 revenue, FQ3 ’26 highlighted. (Source: Estimize)
Flat isn’t as bad as it sounds. Q3 2025 was inflated by US buyers rushing to grab the $7,500 federal tax credit before it expired on September 30, 2025, so matching it without the credit would be a decent result.
But look at the sequential picture. Tesla posted $28.24 billion in revenue in Q2 2026 on 480,126 deliveries and 13.5 GWh of storage. Q3 had more of both, yet Wall Street is modeling slightly less revenue and Estimize only about $120 million more, which means both are baking in lower average selling prices.
Tesla Q3 2026 earnings
Analysts expect non-GAAP earnings per share of $0.45, down 10% from $0.50 in Q3 2025. The Estimize consensus is a little higher at $0.48, and Wall Street estimates range from $0.30 to $0.70.
Wall Street and Estimize consensus for Tesla’s Q3 2026 EPS, FQ3 ’26 highlighted. (Source: Estimize)
Take that number with a grain of salt. In Q2, Tesla came in at $0.33 against a $0.53 consensus, as its operating margin collapsed to 1.4% . Operating income fell 57% to $398 million while operating expenses jumped 47% to $4.35 billion.
Tesla has now missed the Street’s EPS estimate in two of the last four quarters. And its EPS has declined year-over-year in five of the last seven.
The number we’ll be watching first is automotive gross margin excluding regulatory credits. It dropped to 16.3% in Q2 from 19.2% in Q1, which Tesla blamed on a $230 million warranty true-down and tariff relief that helped Q1 and didn’t repeat.
Regulatory credits won’t bail it out either. They brought in only $146 million in Q2, down 67% from a year earlier, and that pure-profit revenue keeps shrinking now that automakers no longer face federal CAFE penalties.
Then there’s cash. Tesla burned $1.09 billion in free cash flow in Q2 as capital expenditures more than doubled to $5.8 billion, and management guided to more than $25 billion in capex for 2026, with spending weighted to the second half. Another negative free cash flow quarter wouldn’t be a surprise.
Energy is worth a look too. The storage business ran a 20.4% gross margin in Q2, and Tesla says it expects the low-to-mid 20% range long term. With Q3 deployments missing estimates by more than 2 GWh, energy won’t offset much.
Most-upvoted Tesla shareholder questions for Q3 2026
Tesla’s Say Technologies Q&A for the call closes today at 4 p.m. ET. It drew 832 questions from about 2,860 participants representing 3.85 million shares.
That’s more people than last quarter (about 1,710) but less than half the shares, which were 8.6 million in Q2.
Here are the top questions ranked by shares represented:
“How does the Cybercab fleet scale past Austin, and what’s the regulatory path outside Texas given NHTSA’s open safety review?” (980 votes, 1.2 million shares)
“When can we anticipate FSD unsupervised in customer cars?” (1,200 votes, 1.1 million shares)
“When will the CyberCab be available for customer purchase/ownership?” (1,100 votes, 952,900 shares)
“What’s the unit economics per paid robotaxi mile, and how does it compare to the thirty-cent target?” (435 votes, 694,900 shares)
When HW3 owners will learn whether they get a free hardware upgrade for unsupervised FSD (557 votes, 652,900 shares)
“What’s the cost per Optimus unit, and what does the first paying customer look like?” (699 votes, 643,600 shares)
Electrek’s Take
The auto business is flat. Deliveries are up 8.8% year-to-date at 1,324,681, which is a real recovery from two years of decline, but Q3 came in below last year and Tesla still sells almost nothing outside of Model 3 and Model Y.
So the quarter comes down to margins and spending. If auto margins ex-credits hold around 16% and opex stops climbing 40%+ a year, the Q2 miss was a one-off. If not, Tesla is spending more than $25 billion this year on AI, Optimus, Cybercab and chips while its core business barely breaks even at the operating level. That’s a car company funding a very expensive bet out of a shrinking profit pool.
And shareholders mostly don’t care. Look at the questions: Cybercab, FSD, Optimus, HW3. The top question about Tesla’s consumer lineup was a request for a van.
They are completely delusional, waiting for questionable new products to bring in money while watching their cash cows stop growing, something that was completely avoidable if Musk hadn’t bet the whole company on autonomy too early.

source_document.body:
Photo: LAZ Parking
Apartment and condo residents could get more places to plug in their EVs without their buildings needing a costly electrical upgrade. LAZ Parking and EverCharge are launching a charging service that shares available power among vehicles – an approach the companies say can support up to five times as many charging ports on the same power supply.
The new service, LAZ Multifamily EV Charging Powered by EverCharge SmartPower, is available across LAZ’s US-wide footprint. EverCharge is a wholly owned subsidiary of indiGOtech, which goes by GO.
For anyone who lives in an apartment or condo, getting a charger installed can involve more than just choosing a parking space. The apartment building’s electrical capacity has to accommodate EV charging, and upgrading the infrastructure can make the project expensive before anyone plugs in.
EverCharge’s SmartPower manages charging output in real time based on how much electricity vehicles need and how much power the site has available. That gives property owners a way to install more chargers within their existing electrical limits, the company says.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The approach spreads the available power across charging vehicles as demand changes. The potential benefit is that more residents can plug in where they already park, with less need for expensive electrical work.
LAZ operates around 2.1 million parking spaces at 5,700 locations in the US and Canada. EverCharge already operates more than 10,000 charging ports at over 1,000 apartment and condo properties, serving more than 50,000 registered drivers.
LAZ says the venture expands its charging network to 25,000 ports across North America. That figure describes its expanded network; the announcement doesn’t set a target or timeline for new apartment and condo installations.
The rollout will use EverCharge’s EVO3 Level 2 chargers. The companies haven’t disclosed resident charging prices or named the first properties getting installations. Beyond residential charging, they also plan to explore charging and battery swapping for commercial fleets, ride-hailing, and delivery services.

source_document.body:
Rivian is now the #2 EV brand in the US, up from 10th last year, taking Chevrolet’s spot as almost every other automaker tries to slow down the inevitable transition to electric cars.
In the last year, the US electric car market has been… volatile, to say the least.
Q3 2025 saw a huge sales jump, in an advance of an effort by US republicans to inflate the price of EVs by $7,500 .
So, looking forward to this year, it was inevitable that we would see a large drop in sales in Q3, since records were set in last Q3.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Sure enough, as sales numbers came in , most brands were down. This is to be expected after incentive expiry – though EV sales have been steadily recovering in the intervening months .
Part of the reason for that recovery has been due to a lot of dumb oil conflicts around the world, causing oil prices to rise to record levels (helped by intentional policy decisions to push them even higher ). As oil prices rise, the already-obvious case for electric transportation becomes all the more clear.
This has caused EV sales to shoot up in the rest of the world. Unfortunately, American access to affordable EVs has been restricted due to dumb tariffs and other barriers intended to keep Americans spending and polluting more.
EV sales could have been higher in the US, but the reason they’ve stayed depressed from previous levels isn’t due to consumer demand, but because automakers are almost universally refusing to make EVs, according to research from UC Davis .
There are a few exceptions, though. With Rivian as the standout among them.
According to Cox Automotive’s new Q3 sales report , almost every brand saw a decrease in EV sales in Q3, with Mercedes, Lexus, Toyota, Subaru, and Rivian as the exceptions.
Each of these brands have new models which helped to bring up sales. Toyota has its improved bZ and new C-HR, Lexus its new ES, Subaru its Trailseeker and Uncharted , Mercedes its CLA, and most importantly, Rivian has its R2.
Meanwhile, many of the brands with falling sales have cancelled models (even ones that were previously their best-sellers ). Unsurprisingly, when Americans are not allowed to buy a car, they won’t buy it.
Rivian’s new R2 is a make-or-break car for the company, a much more affordable, smaller version of its R1S. It just started sales a few months ago, and Rivian hopes to ramp up production, aiming for the same market the Tesla Model Y is in.
The Model Y remains the US’ best-selling EV, but its sales went down year over year as well. Tesla has not so much retreated from EV production, more that its CEO is now spending more money to harm EVs than any other person on the planet . Even with Tesla’s nearly 20% drop in sales year over year, It’s still ahead of the rest of the pack.
But 2nd place used to be taken up by Chevy, which was proud of that fact. It has several capable EV offerings, including the newly-improved, affordable Chevy Bolt (which is, nevertheless, being cancelled next year ). (GM is still second place if you combine all of its brands together, though, but if Rivian’s growth continues, that may or may not hold)

America adopted the metric system in 1866 (true story), with the Congress Act that made it “lawful throughout the United States of America to employ the weights and measures of the metric system in all contracts, dealings or court proceedings.” Still, the land of the free decided against making it the main system, so the Imperial legacy carried on undisturbed (in the most republican establishment of them all). But Detroit occasionally jumped ship and spelled engine displacements in logic units. Remember the 8.2-litre Cadillac Eldorado of 1972?
Foreword: the metric system and grammar have not yet joined in holy matrimony, therefore Brits spell “litre,” and “metre,” while their cousins from across the Atlantic ditched the Frenchy writing altogether, and went phonetically correct (liter, meter). Irrespective of how you inscribe it, it sounds off went put on a Pontiac GTO, a Cadillac Eldorado, or a Dodge Viper. Or any American car, for that matter, especially the ones built when cylinders and cubic inches made perfect sense.
Maybe that’s what they mean by "They don't make them like they used to"? or is it something else entirely? That worn adage usually sounds like lazy nostalgia, yet in 2026, it rings with undisputed truth. Glance at a modern Cadillac showroom filled with whisper-quiet socket-sucking crossovers sculpted by wind tunnels and algorithms, then look back at 1972.
Back then, Detroit built unapologetic personal luxury dreadnoughts, rolling statements of ambition, optimism, and mechanical theater that turned every highway into a grand stage. Yes, I know: the term personal luxury car doesn’t apply to Cadillac – not int same manner that it applies to all other cars of the genre, mostly because… well, aren’t all Cadillacs luxury?
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Still, look at the car starring in the video embedded below (and thank Lou Costabile, Chicago-based car vlogger, who drove seven hours to this car to get it on camera), and tell me what you think of Cadillac’s evolution transformation. The car belongs to Steve Plunkett – the name is familiar to our editorial grounds for many other spectacular Caddies (and other GM gems, too), and that means its impeccable. And drivable.
Plunkett has spent decades assembling an extraordinary collection of Cadillacs that spans the marque's most celebrated eras, turning his Canadian residence into a living museum for the Standard of the World. Among those curated treasures sits a car he has cherished for almost fifteen years: an unrestored 1972 Cadillac Eldorado Coupe.
While enthusiasts automatically associate the early-1970s Eldorado with open-air convertibles, this fixed-roof hardtop commands equal reverence through sheer mass and real estate it occupies at any given moment.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Finished in a lustrous metallic gold that radiates wealth (as if Cadillac wasn’t already oozing “money”), Plunkett's coupe is an authentic time traveler showing just 26,000 original miles on its odometer. Built by General Motors in November 1971, the car wears a distinctive white Halo vinyl roof framed by a strip of gold paint above the side glass, creating the visual illusion that the top floats effortlessly over its Coke-bottle rear quarters.
The gravitas of this golden cruiser is rooted in the lineage of its storied badge. Cadillac introduced the Eldorado for the 1953 model year as an ultra-exclusive Motorama show car. The nameplate endured for 50 years until 2002, spanning a dozen distinct generations and hundreds of thousands of examples built. More to the point, twelve hundreds of thousands (1.25 million), meaning the nameplate averaged 100,000 cars for each generation.
Plunkett's 1972 model belongs to the seventh generation, which debuted in 1971 with monumental proportions and stately styling. Just ahead of the standard rear fender skirts sits a simulated vertical air scoop, a deliberate nod to Plunkett's own 1953 Eldorado convertible. Up front, prominent bumper guards flank an egg-crate grille crowned by the Cadillac script and crest.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile The coupe rolls on reproduction Diamond Back tires featuring period-correct double whitewalls. Underhood, the mechanical heart that set the Eldorado apart from every rival on Earth. Lesser 1972 Cadillacs relied on a 472-cubic-inch (7.7-liter) V8 producing 220 net horsepower. The Eldorado exclusively packed a colossal 500-cubic-inch (“8.2-Litre”) V8 delivering 235 net horsepower and 385 lb-ft (522 Nm).
Paired with a Turbo Hydra-Matic 425 automatic transmission, this engine channeled all that torque to the front wheels through stout half-shafts tucked beside the oil pan. When Plunkett turns the key, the 8.2-liter giant awakens with a gentle body rock and settles into a deep, nautical burble reminiscent of a heavy cruiser idling at the pier.
1972 was a banner year for Detroit's flagship division, which produced 267,787 automobiles. Two-door hardtop coupes reigned as the public's favorite body style, spearheaded by the runaway best-selling Coupe de Ville at 95,280 units. Priced at 7,230 dollars, the Eldorado Coupe found 32,099 buyers, slotting well above the entry-level 5,771-dollar Calais Coupe while trailing the 12,106-dollar Fleetwood Seventy-Five limousine at the top.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Trimmed by Fisher with Fleetwood luxury appointments, the gold interior envelops passengers in plush, six-way power seats that feel like overstuffed club chairs. Expansive woodgrain accents adorn the wide dashboard, which houses a working factory clock, an early cassette tape player, and a perforated temperature sensor regulating the automatic climate control system Cadillac pioneered in 1964.
Perched atop the front fenders and tucked above the rear window are small indicator pods connected directly to the exterior bulbs via fiber-optic light cables. Without using a single transistor, this system lets the driver verify whether headlights, parking lamps, or brake lights are functioning right from the driver's seat, where only the Cadillac crest graces the dash.

Who Owns the World's Most Expensive Car, the Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupe After All?
15 photos
Photo: billionaires_flix | Instagram
The 1955 Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupe sold for a mind-blowing $142 million at an RM Sotheby’s auction back in 2022, making it not only the most expensive Mercedes ever sold, but also the most valuable car in the world. The buyer's identity has never been officially disclosed, but all hints point to one person.
The Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Coupe was not just a fast sports car. It was literally a Grand Prix racing machine modified to support a roof. Mercedes designed and built nine rolling chassis for endurance racing, based on the chassis of the W196 R Formula One car, driven by Juan Manuel Fangio.
However, only two of them were fitted with the closed-top coupe bodies and the striking gullwing doors. The two are affectionately called "The Red" and "The Blue," with reference to the upholstery colors that they came with.
Following the tragic 1955 Le Mans crash that killed 82 people and injured 120 more, Mercedes-Benz pulled out of all competitions, shelving the 300 SLR racing program entirely. With the program cancelled, chief engineer Rudolf Uhlenhaut took one of the two completed prototypes and claimed it as his personal company car. He bolted a massive, suitcase-sized muffler to the side and drove it to work every day.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz | RM Sotheby's The bodywork was handcrafted from Elektron, an incredibly lightweight but highly flammable magnesium alloy. The car weighed a mere 2,200 pounds (998 kilograms). That is how much the 3.0-liter, direct-injection, straight-eight engine had to push forward with the force of 306 horsepower (310 metric horsepower) and 234 pound-feet (317 Newton meters) of torque.
That was enough to make the coupe rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in roughly 7.0 seconds, which was extremely fast for the mid-1950s, and hit a top speed of 180 mph (290 kph). The top speed was actually limited by the very skinny bias-ply tires of the era. However, tests showed that it could do even more.
Back then, standard sports cars struggled to cross 120 mph (193 kph). At a speed of 180 mph, the Mercedes-Benz-badged silver bullet was the fastest road-legal vehicle on Earth by far, a crown that it wore for decades.
All those capabilities were reportedly tested by Mercedes-Benz's brilliant chief engineer, Rudolf Uhlenhaut. The story goes that on the day he needed to attend a meeting in Munich, some 140 miles away from Stuttgart, he woke up late.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz | RM Sotheby's To get there as close as possible to the scheduled time of the meeting, he got in the 3 00 SLR Coupe and pinned the throttle of his company car for a journey in record time. And he did. He completed the 140-mile route on the Autobahn in just over one hour. But how was that even possible?
Back in 1955, Germany's Autobahn network had absolutely no speed limits whatsoever, and traffic was incredibly sparse compared to the traffic of today. Besides, Germany did not even introduce radar speed traps until 1959.
Furthermore, Rudolf Uhlenhaut was not just a corporate executive in a suit. He was a racing genius. During an F1 test session at the Nurburgring, reigning World Champion Juan Manuel Fangio supposedly complained that the car was not set up right.
Uhlenhaut got up from lunch, climbed into the car while wearing his suit and tie, and drove a lap that was 3 seconds faster than Fangio’s, proving that there was nothing really wrong with the setup. However, the story sounds like an exaggerated myth, considering that Fangio was a racing phenomenon. The driver Uhlenhaut reportedly beat in that specific session was actually factory driver Karl Kling.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz | RM Sotheby's To cover that distance in roughly 60 minutes, Rudolf Uhlenhaut had to maintain an average speed of over 135 mph (over 217 kph). This means that he must have frequently pushed the car over the official limit of 180 mph.
The "late for a meeting" excuse was actually a myth fueled by drama over the years, because who wouldn't like to hear an exciting story? The truth was that the high-speed run was actually a calculated engineering test session.
Uhlenhaut frequently commuted between the Daimler headquarters in Stuttgart and Munich, using public roads as his personal proving ground to evaluate the car’s cooling, stability, and reliability under prolonged high-speed stress. Whether it was for a meeting or a test, the actual numbers behind the drive remain mind-boggling for 1955.
For nearly 70 years, Mercedes kept both "The Blue" and "The Red" safely locked away in their museum vaults. But on May 5, 2022, the automaker hosted a secret, invitation-only auction at the Mercedes-Benz Museum in Stuttgart, auctioning off "The Red" car.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz | RM Sotheby's While The Red, chassis 08/55, was Uhlenhaut’s daily company car, the one credited with blasting down the Autobahn from Stuttgart to Munich in approximately one hour, The Blue was primarily kept as a pristine museum piece for decades, but also driven on occasional media events or high-speed tests.
In front of the world’s elite collectors, the 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupe sold for the mind-blowing $142 million , and nobody knows who took it home. The winning bid was placed by a Swiss high-end car broker, Simon Kidston, on behalf of an anonymous private collector, described as a " well-known figure from Britain’s automotive industry and long-standing collector ."
The car was spotted driving randomly in Monte Carlo , making some assume that it might belong to a Formula 1 driver. However, clues point not to a Formula 1 driver, but to someone with strong ties in Formula 1, placing billionaire Sir Jim Ratcliffe as the ultimate candidate.
His net worth is estimated to be approximately $17.6 billion according to tracking by Forbes, ranking him among the world’s top 160 wealthiest individuals. Furthermore, he has close ties to the Mercedes-Benz brand. His company, Ineos, owns a one-third stake in the Mercedes- AMG Petronas F1 Team, alongside Mercedes-Benz and Toto Wolff , so he isn't just a customer, but part of the team's exclusive shareholding trio.
Photo: billionaires_flix | Instagram Mercedes sold the car to someone who would be able to check its boxes. The strict terms of the sale require the owner to regularly make it available for public exhibition and special events. As an automotive figure and founder of his own car brand, Sir Jim Ratcliffe obviously possesses the means to store, maintain, and display the most expensive car in the world, just as Mercedes-Benz demanded.

A. Duie Pyle has opened a 44-door less-than-truckload (LTL) service center in the Cincinnati area, expanding its direct freight network in southwest Ohio just two weeks after opening a nearly 79,000-square-foot warehouse in central Pennsylvania.
The two most recent openings follow other investments aimed at expanding Pyle’s transportation and distribution capabilities beyond its traditional Northeast stronghold.
In January, FreightWaves reported that Pyle had acquired a 43-acre site at the Port 460 Logistics Center in Suffolk, Virginia, near the Port of Virginia.
Pyle has also expanded into U.S.–Mexico cross-border freight transportation over the last year.
The West Chester, Pennsylvania-based carrier announced Tuesday that the new service center in Cincinnati will strengthen freight connections between the Midwest region and its established Northeast and Mid-Atlantic markets.
The 44-door service center in the Cincinnati market extends Pyle’s direct less-than-truckload network into Southwest Ohio. (Photo: A. Duie Pyle)
The Cincinnati facility is expected to create 21 jobs initially, with employment projected to reach approximately 36 by the end of 2026, according to the company.
“Growing our network is about being where our customers need us and creating stronger connections between the markets they serve,” Frank Granieri, chief commercial officer at A. Duie Pyle, said in a news release.
The opening is part of a broader westward expansion strategy announced in 2025, when Pyle outlined plans to establish additional service centers in Ohio to improve transit times and reduce its reliance on partner carriers.
In March 2025, John Luciani, Pyle’s chief operating officer for LTL operations, told FreightWaves the company was pursuing new terminals in Columbus, Toledo and Cincinnati to expand its direct overnight service footprint.
The carrier had acquired a former Yellow Corp. terminal in Bowling Green, Ohio, to serve the Toledo market and leased a facility in Columbus as part of that expansion.
The Cincinnati opening advances that strategy by bringing more freight movements in southwest Ohio directly into Pyle’s network, potentially reducing intermediate transfers and improving service consistency.
The Cincinnati opening follows Pyle’s Oct. 6 announcement of a new 78,760-square-foot warehouse in Camp Hill, Pennsylvania.
The Camp Hill warehouse sits adjacent to the company’s existing LTL service center, creating an integrated logistics campus that combines freight transportation and inventory storage.
The Camp Hill facility provides access to several major freight corridors, including Interstates 81, 76 and 83 and U.S. Route 15.
Pyle said the location is particularly suited for customers in healthcare, medical supplies and manufacturing that require consistent inventory availability and just-in-time replenishment.
Founded in 1924, A. Duie Pyle is a privately held, family-owned transportation and logistics company offering LTL trucking, dedicated transportation, warehousing and brokerage services.
Why it matters: A. Duie Pyle’s investments strengthen the company’s direct-service capabilities in Ohio while expanding its ability to combine transportation and warehousing across the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic.

source_document.body:
The artificial intelligence industry is obsessed with increasing speed and scale. Faster processors. Larger models. More GPUs. Bigger AI factories.
Yet the uncomfortable truth is that even small amounts of packet loss can significantly degrade the performance of some of the world’s most advanced and expensive computing resources.
That is the paradox at the heart of modern AI infrastructure.
The industry is assembling vast systems containing tens of thousands of GPUs, only to discover that their collective performance depends on their ability to communicate with extraordinary precision. The individual processor may be a technological marvel, but AI training is ultimately a team sport. During synchronized collective operations, progress is often gated by the slowest participant, so a delayed GPU or data transfer can hold up the group, and waiting is expensive.
To understand how the industry arrived here, it helps to consider how increasingly sophisticated model training has changed traffic patterns.
(BLACKDAY/Shutterstock)
A modern training job distributes work across many GPUs, which repeatedly exchange data such as gradients, parameters or activations before proceeding to the next step. The resulting traffic is highly synchronized, exceptionally bursty and overwhelmingly east-west. Thousands of processors may reach the same synchronization barrier at nearly the same time, exchange information and then wait until every member of the group is ready to continue. Essentially, the network today is an integral part of the AI computing system.
The First Generation of AI Ethernet
Ethernet has continually adapted to new demands, and AI training has accelerated that evolution.
One of the industry’s first major responses was RDMA over Converged Ethernet, or RoCEv2. It enables endpoints to transfer data directly between application memory regions over an Ethernet and IP network, bypassing much of the conventional operating-system networking path. By reducing processing overhead and latency, RoCEv2 made Ethernet far better suited to synchronized communication between GPUs.
However, moving data quickly was only part of the challenge. It was equally important to manage congestion and limit packet loss. Technologies such as Priority Flow Control (PFC) can temporarily pause upstream transmission for traffic in a priority class before buffers on the receiving side overflow. Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) allows switches to mark packets as congestion builds, enabling endpoint congestion-control mechanisms to reduce their transmission rates in response.
The physical architecture evolved too. In many large AI clusters, general-purpose leaf-spine designs have been complemented or replaced by rail-optimized fabrics, in which GPU interfaces are mapped to dedicated network planes. These designs can provide greater traffic isolation, resilience and predictability.
This combination worked remarkably well. Ethernet had once again reinvented itself to address a new class of applications.
Ethernet is widely used with clusters (Photo by Sanjay Suchak, UVA Communications)
But as clusters expanded, GPU-to-GPU communication increased in both volume and complexity. Congestion became harder to manage, loss recovery remained costly, configuration became more complex and implementations of congestion-avoidance techniques often varied across vendors. Approaches designed for one generation of clusters began to strain under the ambitions of the next.
The problem was no longer simply how to build a faster network. It was how to orchestrate enormous volumes of synchronized traffic without allowing that traffic to collide with itself.
From Avoiding to Outmaneuvering Congestion
The industry’s next response represented a change in philosophy.
Traditional networks commonly assign each flow to a selected path, while dynamic load balancing can move flows, or flowlets, across the fabric while seeking to limit packet reordering. Emerging AI transports go further by allowing packets from the same communication stream to use multiple paths simultaneously and treating out-of-order arrival as an expected transport condition.
The Ultra Ethernet Consortium (UEC) advanced this approach through Ultra Ethernet Transport (UET), the transport layer defined in the Ultra Ethernet architecture. UET can distribute packets from the same communication stream across multiple paths while allowing the receiving endpoint to handle out-of-order arrival.
This is an important conceptual shift, as instead of responding only after congestion develops, the transport can use more of the available fabric and reduce the likelihood that individual links become bottlenecks.
The Open Compute Project’s (OCP’s) Multipath Reliable Connection (MRC) specification defines a new open RDMA transport for AI training fabrics with per-packet multipath operation, enhanced congestion control and faster loss recovery. MRC uses mechanisms including entropy-based packet spraying and SRv6 source routing to distribute and steer traffic across available network paths. Meta has pursued similar goals through MetaRoCE, a clean-sheet RDMA transport designed for AI-scale Ethernet.
Connecting accelerators remains a challenge (Aldobarettoow/Shutterstock)
Although these approaches differ, they point in the same direction: AI fabrics are becoming increasingly multipath, telemetry-rich and responsive to workload requirements. Responsibility for path selection, congestion management and loss recovery is increasingly shared between the network and the systems connected to it.
This evolution is unlikely to end with the adoption of a single protocol. AI architectures are changing too quickly for the industry to declare the problem solved. The enduring requirement is therefore not allegiance to one transport mechanism, but a networking foundation that can adapt as those mechanisms evolve. That foundation must provide predictable connectivity, rich telemetry and real-time congestion awareness, while enabling endpoint technologies to use network resources intelligently.
Ethernet’s advantage is the breadth of the ecosystem beneath those protocols: interoperable switching, standardized physical layers, operational familiarity and a large multivendor supply base. That foundation allows transport and congestion-control mechanisms to evolve without requiring the industry to abandon the infrastructure around them.
The Beast Is Leaving the Factory
Even this is not the end of the story.
Much of the industry’s attention has focused on training and the construction of hyperscale AI factories. Training creates the models that have captured the world’s imagination. But inference is what allows those models to answer questions, make recommendations, automate workflows, generate content and control physical systems.
As AI services move toward widespread commercial deployment, AI infrastructure is likely to become more distributed, particularly where workload placement is influenced by latency, data sovereignty, resilience or power availability. Enterprises, governments, developers and cloud providers will increasingly access high-performance computing through GPU-as-a-Service (GPUaaS) and related models rather than build every capability themselves. AI resources will be spread across central, regional and edge facilities, placed according to application requirements rather than a fixed architectural model.
AI fabrics are emerging to handle networking for AI clusters (Bolbik/Shutterstock)
The resulting system will be far more complex than an isolated GPU cluster. Compute, data platforms, memory, specialized accelerators, inference engines and cached context may reside in different facilities and under different administrative domains. Data, models and context will therefore need to move securely and efficiently across facilities, operators and network boundaries.
The network must therefore evolve from connecting processors inside an AI factory to connecting intelligence across an AI economy.
At this point, the implications extend beyond infrastructure performance. Distributed AI will underpin services such as intelligent manufacturing, warehouse automation, predictive maintenance, healthcare diagnostics and autonomous transportation. In these environments, the network will not simply carry the output of an AI service. Its performance, resilience and operational agility will materially influence the service’s responsiveness, availability and ability to operate at scale.
The AI training beast has taught us a valuable lesson: compute cannot scale independently of connectivity. Each new generation of processors creates a corresponding challenge for the network, and every expansion of AI into the physical economy further raises the stakes.
The future will belong not merely to those who assemble the largest collections of GPUs, but to those who can make distributed compute, data and memory resources behave as one intelligent system. Ethernet’s next chapter will be defined by its ability to provide the adaptable, observable and resilient connectivity that makes that system possible.
That is the next frontier for Ethernet—and the challenge that will shape AI’s continued expansion.

China-Built Tesla Model 3 Premium Hit With Safety Recall, Over 131,000 Units Affected
20 photos
Photo: Tesla
The world's premier electric vehicle manufacturer has issued a recall affecting a bunch of Model 3 Premium sedans produced at Gigafactory Shanghai for three regions. More specifically, the 131,726-strong recall population ended up in the European Union, the Middle East, and South Korea, with said population comprising left-hand-drive sedans exclusively.
Per the report published via the European Commission's Safety Gate rapid alert system, the far-side airbag software can push shoulder loading past the mandated limit in a side impact. More to the point, recalled vehicles may exceed a lateral force of 3.0 kN on the shoulder during a pole collision.
Being a software-only issue, its fix arrives over the air, just as expected from such a tech-infused vehicle. Remedy software changes how the airbag deploys. Tesla calls the campaign SB-26-00-006, which is otherwise known as SR/02850/26 in Safety Gate speak. The regulation at the center of this recall is UN R135, which applies to nearly all new car type approvals worldwide.
In said test, a pole strikes the driver's door at 32 kilometers per hour (20 miles per hour), with the driver's seat being occupied by a WorldSID crash test dummy. As noted earlier, the lateral force on the dummy's left shoulder cannot exceed 3,000 Newtons. Under standard Earth gravity, that is the amount of downward force exerted by a 306-kilogram (674-pound) mass. Big yikes!
Needless to say, the pole-type side impact is the kind of crash scenario where a narrow object concentrates force into a small area of the door, increasing the risk of injury. Also known as a center or front-center airbag, the far-side airbag was designed specifically to stop the occupant from sliding across the struck area.
Photo: Tesla Tesla says it had traced excess load to the software calibration of that airbag's deployment strategy. In other words, the airbag does not deploy in a way that keeps the shoulder loading within the regulatory limit during the pole test. The remedy calibration file is included in software versions 2026.26.100.2, 2026.32.3, or later.
Tesla's own service bulletin, which predated the Safety Gate report, lists Model 3 Premium vehicles produced between June 30, 2024, and May 8, 2026, in left-hand drive at the automaker's Chinese vehicle assembly plant. Service technicians are presented with two correction codes in said bulletin.
S012600006 means no update is necessary, while S02260006 indicates that the vehicle has to be updated. That being said, the Model 3 continues to live in the shadow of the Model Y as far as worldwide sales are concerned. The real tragedy here isn't that customers prefer crossover, but that the Model 3 is the more efficient and sleeker-looking vehicle of the rear-biased siblings.
Still one of the highest-volume electric vehicles in the world, the Model 3 carries a starting price of 36,990 euros in Germany for the most basic of specifications. The Model 3 Premium is 44,990 euros from the outset, whereas the Model 3 Performance can be yours from 58,490 before taxes, incentives, and extras.
While it may not be as quick or fast as the Performance, the Premium is the best pick of the bunch in terms of driving range. In the WLTP, it can go up to 750 kilometers (466 miles) on a full charge. Opting for the dual-motor setup results in a WLTP rating of 660 kilometers (410 miles).

source_document.body:
Meta this week released details on Prometheus, the New Albany, Ohio-based supercluster that it used to train Muse, its latest family of AI model. The information is useful, if only to catch a glimpse of how HPC can evolve when price is no object.
As a supercluster, Prometheus is composed of multiple individual clusters that have been integrated to work on massive training jobs. In this case, according to a blog post shared by the Facebook parent on October 20, Meta combined two clusters based on Nvidia’s Grace Blackwell technology, dubbed Catalina and Clemente, with a third platform based on Nvidia Vera Rubin chips, dubbed San Miguel, which is expected to join the party soon.
Catalina is based on Nvidia’s GB200 chip and the NVL72 architecture. Meta devised its own a two-rack configuration, dubbed Ariel, where 36 GPUs per rack are interconnected via NVLink to form a unified 72-GPU domain.
For every GB200 superchip containing a Grace CPU and a Blackwell GPU in Catalina, Meta uses two ConnectX-7 400G NICs, giving it 800G of I/O per GPU “earlier than the rest of the industry,” the Meta engineers write in the blog post.
The second cluster, Clemente, is also based on the NVL72 scale-up architecture. It uses GB300, the Blackwell Ultra chip from Nvidia, which brings 50% more HBM capacity and roughly the same amount of FP4 capacity.
The third cluster, San Miguel, will be based on Vera Rubin NVL72, which utilize the new Vera Rubin GPUs. Meta says it’s looking forward to the 10% to 20% improvement in performance-per-watt compared to GB300 NVL72.
Meta selected Nvidia’s ConnectX-8 SuperNICs, which deliver 800G per GPU natively. This allowed Meta to utilize a two-to-one GPU-to-CPU ratio and therefore to utilize the full NLV72 rack to house the full complement of 72 GPUs, instead of splitting the GPUs across two racks, as it did with Catalina.
Meta connects Catalina and Clemente used Ethernet-based interconnects that can link up to 20,736 GPUs “through a high-bandwidth, low-latency multi-layer topology,” the Meta engineers write.
The first iteration of the network fabric used a Disaggregated Scheduled Fabric (DSF), which uses “sub-packet-level multipath routing and packet re-ordering” in the fabric, “along with virtual output queues and credit-based end-to-end flow control” to mitigate network congestion.
The second iteration moved to Non-Scheduled Fabric (NSF), which were based on “shallow-buffer 51.2T Ethernet switches” that provided dynamic load balancing, such as Minipack3, the third-generation switch Meta designed and contracted Celestica to manufacture. It also utilizes Minipack3N, another Meta designed switch, manufactured by Accton. Minipack3N is based on Nvidia’s Spectrum-4 switch ASIC and adds Nvidia’s adaptive routing technology.
“Both DSF and NSF are based on Meta’s FBOSS networking stack, giving us the control to rapidly iterate on and optimize the fabrics in Prometheus, and the visibility to operate these clusters at scale,” Meta’s engineers write.
Prometheus also consists of a Backend Aggregation (BAG) network. According to Meta, the BAG network is based on a multi-layer hub-and-spoke network that connects clusters residing between a distance of 2 kilometer to 100 kilometers. The BAG network is built with Arista 7800-series chassis “running deep-buffered Broadcom Jericho3 silicon, delivering multiple Pbps of bandwidth per region pair,” Meta writes.
“Running pretraining over this network required a dedicated optimization effort with Meta Superintelligence Labs to ensure training was not slowed down, especially given speed-of-light constraints at these distances,” they write.
Meta’s Backend Aggregation (BAG) connects buildings 2 km to 100 km apart
All told, Meta’s network is composed of millions of miles of fiber strand, tens of thousands of switches, and millions of optics.
Moving from NVL8 to NVL72 allowed Meta to greatly increase the size of its scale-up cluster and therefore amount of data it could keep in memory at a single time while maintaining tensor parallelism. However, it also increased the “blast radius” of a hardware fault by 9x.
To help alleviate concerns of hardware failures, Meta keeps eight of the GPUs in each NVL72 domain offline. In the event that one of the 64 functioning GPUs fails, one of the eight hot spares jumps into action and the job is immediately restarted at the last checkpoint.
It does something similar at the rack level, keeping 2% of its racks offline as hot spares. “For a 32,768 active-GPU training run, this means provisioning 523 NVL72 racks, or 37,656 GPUs, about 13% above the active footprint,” the company writes. “Most of that margin (11%) falls out of the 64-of-72 slice geometry rather than being an absolute reliability tax.”
Maintaining integrity at the chip level is another thing entirely. While this is largely Nvidia’s domain, Meta engineers also have their fingerprints on the project, seeing as how its their bacon on the line if things go south.
“A single NVL72 domain incorporates 5,184 tuned differential-pair signaling links operating at 200 Gbps, each traversing multiple potential points of failure, including GPU SerDes, compute tray PCBs, cable cartridges, and switch tray interfaces,” the Meta engineers write. “Maintaining consistent signal integrity across this dense fabric–at 200 Gbps per lane–represents an unprecedented engineering challenge at this scale.”
Meta implemented a pair of fault recovery mechanisms that it used for Prometheus (and likely other clusters), including Parallelism-Aware Fault Tolerance (PAFT), which kicks in when a fault can be isolated to a data-parallel model replica, and distributed checkpointing, when it can’t.
San Miguel will be based on Vera Rubin NVL72
Meta has lowered the rate of faults on Prometheus since it started rolling it out in mid-2025. At that time, it experienced nearly 1,000 faults per 8K GPUs daily. Since then, it has lowered the number of interruptions by 99%, and is approaching the goal of two faults per 8K GPUs daily.
Managing electricity consumption is another aspect of Prometheus where Meta learned some lessons. Electrical loads can suddenly vary by 30% to 40%, accounting for tens of megawatts of load swing, thanks to a single job. To address this, Meta developed something called Dynamo Dimmer, which allows it to cap power consumption by slowly adjusting GPU power consumption as it nears its electrical ceiling.
Catalina and Clemente both use liquid cooling. Meta has adopted direct-to-chip and closed-loop liquid cooling to ensure that its not consuming water that could be used by the greater New Albany community.

Tahoma E Is a Rugged, Off-Grid Expedition Camper Built for Round-the-World Adventures
24 photos
Photo: Overland Van Project
If you are the kind of outdoor lover whose adventures involve dropping off the grid and exploring the four corners of the world, you certainly need a rig that is built tough and capable of handling difficult terrain, while also offering comfort and practicality on long trips.
Overland Van Project’s latest creation is designed for exactly this kind of travel. Built on a Ford E-450 cutaway chassis and christened Tahoma E, this new expedition vehicle is a purpose-built overlanding beast that combines a heavy-duty chassis and four-wheel-drive capability with generous payload capacity and a comfortable living space.
Based in Milwaukie, Oregon, Overland Van Project has been around since 2017 and specializes in adventure vehicles, such as high-end camper vans, expedition trucks, and off-grid rigs capable of taking people beyond paved roads and conventional campsites.
According to the builder, the new Tahoma E is designed to bridge the gap between camper vans and heavy-duty global expedition trucks. As such, instead of converting a standard cargo van, the project starts with a Ford E-450 cutaway chassis and adds a fully bonded composite habitation box on top. Measuring 23.5 feet (7.16 meters) in length and 7 feet (2.1 meters) in width, this rig basically has the footprint of a 170” Sprinter van, but offers the rugged capability of a massive off-road truck.
Photo: Overland Van Project The Ford E-450 cutaway chassis is powered by a 7.3-liter Godzilla V8 gasoline engine producing 350 hp. To give the vehicle the confidence to tackle some of the world’s toughest terrain , the team at Overland Van Project (OVP) fitted it with a U-Joint 4x4 conversion, paired with heavy-duty axles, upgraded suspension, and a six-inch lift with airbag leveling.
The tuned shocks optimize damping and articulation for smoother rides over any type of terrain, and the vehicle rolls on custom 19.5-inch Pariah Highline Super Single aluminum wheels wrapped in 37-inch Founders all-terrain tires rated for 6,500 pounds (1,633 kg).
But one of the things OVP seems to be most proud of is the engineered zero-torsion subframe. Most conventional camper van bodies are relatively rigid, which can create problems when the chassis twists over uneven surfaces. The builder didn’t want this to happen, so Tahoma E’s subframe is designed to allow up to 22 degrees of articulation, keeping all four tires in contact with the ground no matter the circumstances. This improves traction, stability, and control, especially when traversing off-chamber sections.
Photo: Overland Van Project The habitation box attached to this mighty chassis is a four-season camper unit built with premium R11-rated composite panels for durability and year-round usability. It offers a 14-foot (4.2-meter) floor area inside, with 6.75 feet (2 meters) of interior width and 7 feet (2.13 meters) of headroom, creating a relatively open living space.
To maintain a light overall weight, OVP used an aluminum structure, with custom cabinetry built from lightweight marine-grade materials that won’t warp or delaminate. A slatted ceiling with integrated LED strips create a nice, warm ambiance, and numerous dual-pane windows bring in plenty of natural light.
In terms of interior layout, future owners can choose between two configurations, called Hauler and Lounger, aimed at different traveling styles. As the name suggests, the Hauler is designed for adventurers who need secure storage space for bringing along mountain bikes and other bulky gear. It features a four-person face-to-face dinette with a lengthwise queen-size drop-down bed above it and a generous rear garage that can hold two bikes.
Photo: Overland Van Project The Lounger, on the other hand, is for people who prioritize living comfort. With this configuration, they get a spacious U-shaped dinette under a widthwise queen-size elevator bed, along with a smaller garage for storage. So regardless of the model you choose, you get the elevator bed, which makes better use of the available space.
The dinette benches come with waterproof micro suede cushions and a hexagonal central table. It also converts into a bed at night, and there is also an overcab bed with a slide-out section for extra sleeping capacity. All three beds are queen-size and come with comfortable 4-inch RomeRest mattresses.
The Tahoma E is designed with an open cab, allowing for easy passage between the driver’s cockpit and the living space, and the seating arrangements are also flexible. Apart from the cab seats, owners can add two extra swiveling passenger seats with three-point harnesses in the habitation area.
The kitchen boasts custom, rattle-free cabinets and a white solid surface countertop and is equipped with a sink, a two-burner induction cooktop, an Isotherm refrigerator, and a microwave convection oven.
Photo: Overland Van Project There is also an indoor wet bathroom for added convenience long journeys . It comes with a standard shower and a CompoCloset S1 sealing and diverting toilet, but customers can opt for an Infinity recirculating shower.
Off-grid independence is another strong suit of the Tahoma E. A 1,000Ah, 12-volt Victron lithium battery bank, equivalent to approximately 13kWh of nominal energy storage, supports off-grid air conditioning, induction cooking, and everyday electronics. The system also includes 1,000 watts of solar panels and a 3,000-watt inverter/charger.
Four-season comfort is ensured by a Velit 2000R 12-volt air conditioner, while a Rixen hydronic system provides heating and domestic hot water. The expedition camper also carries a 53-gallon (200-liter) fresh water tank with heated envelope and a 20-gallon (75-liter) gray-water tank.
The Tahoma E expedition vehicle has a gross vehicle weight of 14,500 pounds (6,577 kg), with a listed curb weight of 12,500 pounds (5,670 kg), resulting in about 2,000 pounds (907 kg) of payload capacity. The rig is RVIA-certified and comes with a premium base price of $330,000. The builder mentions that financing is available through most banks.

1975 Hurst/Olds Is Dressed To Impress, Packs W30 Power
14 photos
Photo: MGM CLASSIC CARS/YouTube
Introduced in 1968, the Hurst/Olds is arguably the most iconic muscle car produced by GM's mid-priced division. The original Hurst/Olds remained in production for only two years but returned between 1972 and 1975, with additional revivals in 1979 and 1983-1984.
The Hurst/Olds is a rare classic regardless of the year. Although production increased significantly in 1975, sales never exceeded 3,500 examples per year. Overall, Oldsmobile sold only 16,537 Hurst-branded vehicles over nine model years.
The first-year 1968 version is arguably the rarest, with 515 units made. The 1969 Hurst was built in just 906 examples, while 1972 saw only 633 cars roll off the showroom floor. These are also the most desirable iterations of the Hurst/Olds, mainly because they were true muscle cars in terms of oomph.
The Hurst you see here left the assembly line in 1975, at a time when muscle cars were a thing of the past. In fact, this is the first iteration of the series equipped with catalytic converters. It was also the first based on the formal roofed Cutlass Supreme coupe (instead of the fastback S model) and the first with a T-top roof.
Drivetrain-wise, the 1975 Hurst/Olds had the same powerplants as its predecessor. The car came standard with the W25 unit, which was a 350-cubic-inch (5.7-liter) small-block V8 rated at 170 horsepower. Output dropped from 180 horsepower in 1974.
The already iconic W30, which displaced a massive 455 cubic inches (7.5 liters), was on the options list and delivered 190 horsepower. The mill was rated at 230 horsepower the previous year. The engines mated with Turbo Hydra-Matic gearboxes, with the W30 featuring a heavy-duty version.
Although it may not be the most potent Hurst/Olds out there, this 1975 coupe is a noteworthy classic, mainly because it looks like it just left the assembly line. There's no info on whether it was restored, but it sure looks like it got a proper overhaul in recent years. It has shiny black paint, a pristine vinyl top, and squeaky-clean white upholstery. Needless to say, the W30 engine is also detailed to nearly as-new condition.
This Olds is also pretty rare. 1975 was the first year when production exceeded 2,000 units. Specifically, the company delivered 2,535 cars. Oldsmobile offered two colors, and records show this coupe is one of 1,242 examples painted Ebony Black (the other 1,293 were finished in Cameo White).
As for the engine, you're looking at one of 1,193 examples optioned up with the 455-cubic-inch W30 V8. There's no info on how many of these cars were black, but the statistic above indicates a near 50-50 split. All told, it might be one of fewer than 600 units with this drivetrain/color combo.
If you're looking for a restored Hurst/Olds that doesn't brake the bank, and you're fine with the low output, this coupe is currently waiting for a new owner in the MGM Classic Cars showroom . It's priced at $36,995.

( Image: Phoenix Tailings. )
Posted By: Mining.com Staff October 20, 2026
Phoenix Tailings plans to build a $375-million (C$527.2-million) commercial-scale rare earths processing facility in Rochester, western New York to process more than 18,000 tons of both mined and recycled rare earth feedstock annually.
The plant, called Freedom Separation, is to produce more than 4,400 tons per year of separated rare earth oxides at its full capacity. Production is expected to ramp up in 2027 before reaching full capacity in 2028. Phoenix operates rare earth metallization facilities in Exeter, N.H., and Burlington, Mass., with production capabilities covering neodymium-praseodymium and heavy rare earth metals. The company has not disclosed the specific mix of rare earth oxides planned for Rochester.
“Technology can give America control over its critical supply chains, but it takes skilled, determined people to turn that promise into production,” Phoenix Tailings CEO and co-founder Nick Myers said in a release on Tuesday. “Rochester has those people. They know how to build, how to innovate, and how to run world-class industrial operations.”
Phoenix joins a growing number of companies developing rare earth processing plants in the United States, including Aclara Resources (TSX: ARA), which plans to begin construction of a Louisiana plant early next year that would process rare earths mined at its projects in Brazil and Chile. Washington seeks to overcome one of the industry’s biggest obstacles: a shortage of domestic facilities capable of separating and refining rare earths needed for magnets, electric vehicles and defence equipment.
Federal backing
The Rochester facility forms part of Phoenix Tailings’ $1.2-billion Freedom project, a separation and metallization platform designed to close the gap in U.S. midstream rare earth processing capacity.
The broader initiative is slated to generate more than 500 jobs across New York, Massachusetts and New Hampshire.
The Freedom Project has secured a $500-million conditional loan commitment from the Department of War’s Office of Strategic Capital under President Donald Trump’s administration.
Leveraging local infrastructure
Phoenix selected Eastman Business Park in Rochester for the 46,500-sq.-metre facility, citing its existing industrial infrastructure and local expertise in engineering, manufacturing, chemical processing and operations.
The project is expected to support more than 200 direct jobs in New York when fully operational, with at least 90 when it launches.
New York governor Kathy Hochul said the state will provide $3 million in performance-based tax credits for the project, Reuters reported.

Apple announced new agreements with U.S. suppliers, including a commitment of up to $100 million over three years with Pennsylvania titanium producer Perryman Company. The metal will go into Apple products, including the iPhone Duo, its first foldable phone.

Apple is also expanding its work with Delaware-based Qnity Electronics, which will manufacture films used in the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera system. Both partnerships are part of Apple’s American Manufacturing Program, launched last year.
The announcement covers materials and components for Apple’s latest phones. Apple says American companies produce nearly 100 components used in the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, drawing from suppliers in more than a dozen states.
“We’re thrilled to expand our work with companies producing advanced materials and components for our newest iPhone lineup right here in America,” said Sabih Khan, Apple’s chief operating officer.

Perryman, a family-owned manufacturer, melts, forges, and rolls titanium at its facility in Houston, Pennsylvania. The titanium it supplies for the iPhone Duo contains at least 80% recycled material and is used in the phone’s grade 5 titanium enclosure.
Qnity’s films will be used in the iPhone 18 Pro’s variable aperture camera system, which adjusts how much light enters the camera. The company joined Apple’s American Manufacturing Program in March.
Apple did not disclose the value of the expanded Qnity agreement or production volumes for either supplier. The manufacturing program is part of its previously announced $600 billion, four-year commitment to U.S. manufacturing and innovation .

Apple also provided updates on several existing suppliers, including projects involving glass, wireless components, and semiconductor production:
Corning: By the end of 2026, its Harrodsburg, Kentucky, facility will produce all cover glass for iPhones and Apple Watches sold worldwide.

TSMC : Its Arizona factory is producing more than 100 million chips for Apple in 2026.

Chip packaging and training
Apple will also be among the first customers of Amkor Technology’s semiconductor packaging and testing facility in Peoria, Arizona. Amkor broke ground in September 2025 and began building the facility’s shell this year; the first two phases are expected to create more than 3,500 local jobs .

6 New Hot Wheels To Think of for Your Collection
27 photos
Photo: Mattel
I just started working on my final scale model car unboxing story for October. After going for Matchbox and Tarmac Works in the first two ones, I figured I’d move on to Hot Wheels. I found 10 items that are over 20 years old, and opening them felt like using a time machine.
Right now I’m almost all set for both November and December, with over 40 tiny cars to go through. I’ve got Mini GT, Kaido House, IXO, Maisto, Matchbox and Hot Wheels on my list. And I know that for 2027 I want to start looking at brands like Greenlight, BBR, and Autoworld.
Just as Mattel comes up with so many new models each year, I’m sure there’s plenty to explore over at those other manufacturers as well. Meanwhile, I’ve just seen the first few photos of the upcoming Porsche 911 Carrera T Super Treasure Hunt with wheels on.
The last time I talked about it, it was just the shell, and it didn’t feel nearly as exciting as it does now. Seeing these 10-spoke Real Riders makes me forget what I said about the livery, and I can see how many collectors will be doing their best to either find this car in the wild or source it from eBay. You’ll have to wait several months before that, though.
If you need a quick fix, I’ve got something for you towards the end of this story. Let’s focus on the next Fast and Furious set first. I don’t know about you but I’ve lost all faith in this theme. Mattel is just taking things too far, and you can easily tell how most enthusiasts feel about it by simply reading the online comments.
Photo: Hot Wheels Malaysia I understand the commercial reasoning behind the plan, but it seems like it’s all downhill from here. We had four Silver Series waves in 2026: Tokyo Drift, Dream Lineup, Race-Off and Silver Anniversary. That’s a total of 20 cars: do you want to guess how many of them I bought? The answer is 0.
Next year is already off to a strange start with “Nitro Grid” looking like Fast and Furious collided with Neon Speeders . “Fast Life” is just as confusing, and now it seems that the third of four potential waves will shift the theme into “Boost Mode”.
That’s an odd choice considering at least two of the vehicles in here are running on naturally-aspirated engines. You could just go with the flow and ignore that information considering the liveries aren’t accurate either. The '11 Dodge Charger R/T is #1 of 5 for the set, and I had forgotten Brendon Vetuskey designed this.
It debuted in 2011 and already rose to fame the following year by joining the Super Treasure Hunt series. Its first Fast and Furious iteration arrived in 2013. It went through a Batman phase between 2020 and 2025, with just one Color Shifters release in 2023. I guess you could be happy about seeing it on a new set of Silver Series wheels.
Photo: Hot Wheels Malaysia Or you could ask where Han’s Veilside RX-7 is after all these years of waiting for it. Leon’s Nissan Skyline is next in line, and what used to be a cool early 2000s livery is currently just barely recognizable. I’m being particularly nitpicky about this one as it was one of my favorite cars in the first movie.
This will be its fifth time paying tribute to that vehicle, whereas we’ve only had one variation for the Tokyo Drift R33 (back in 2020). The Datsun 240Z was part of Fast X, and it first showed up in the 2023 Fast & Furious (Series 3) set where it was easily eclipsed by Neela’s Mazda RX-8.
It abandoned the basic 10-spoke wheels for a set of newer MM5 ones in 2025, and that was almost seemed like the last of it. Look at it and mark my words: it has the potential to be this set’s unofficial peg-warmer. The Nissan Silvia S13 is the only item in the mix that I might consider buying, even though I already have one at home.
The one I’m talking about was part of last year’s Fast & Furious 5-Pack, which uses a set of basic PR5 rims. The Star 5-Spoke design is quite a bit nicer by comparison. And seeing that I don’t even remember seeing this car in any of the movies, I don’t mind the change of livery. I might even agree with the new look on Mia’s Integra, if only for the Fuchs-inspired wheels.
Photo: Mattel There’s a good chance this will be the “Chase” item for the set, as it has only ever had a metal base so far. Anyway, this whole set will be cheaper then Mattel’s upcoming “special trick”, the Hot Wheels R/C 1:64 Subaru Impreza Rally (complete with a 555 number plate and working lights). I haven’t played with any of the company’s remote-controlled vehicles before, and I think it’s just too small to have some serious fun with it.
It’s unlikely it could perform in your backyard, and I wouldn’t like to just try using it on my desktop. I’ve heard some pretty rough stories about the Lamborghini Temerario RC previously, to the point where it might be more than just rumors. Don’t mind me though, you can try to get yours on October 23 , 2026 at 9 AM PT, if you’re OK with paying $55 (before taxes) for it.

Back After 30 Years: 1969 Ford Mustang Mach 1 Left To Rot in a Yard Needs Total Restoration
23 photos
Photo: eBay seller david159043
The Mach 1 continues to be one of the most intriguing restoration projects, and this 1969 specimen is living proof. The car has been sitting for over three decades, but this doesn’t mean it’s a wreck. It’s still a solid restoration candidate, and that’s specifically why it’s here.
The car was posted on eBay, where the owner is trying to let it go after keeping it for all these years in their yard.
It does suffer from obvious problems, but the seller didn’t share more information, so calling them would be a good place to start before making an offer.
Photo: eBay seller david159043 The first thing that probably catches everybody’s attention is the Mach 1 promise. This isn’t a regular Mustang, but a Mach 1 , and we all know what the Mach 1 represented in 1969.
This was the year when the Mach 1 came to be, almost immediately turning the Mustang GT into a configuration that barely made sense. The final production numbers for the 1969 model year speak for themselves, as Ford shipped 72,458 Mach 1s to buyers in the United States and only 5,396 Mustang GTs.
Ford didn’t necessarily consider this a problem, as the Mach 1 proving such a popular model almost overnight paved the way for growing sales in the following model years. However, the Mach 1 still couldn’t help the Mustang sales go up, with Ford ending the year with 299,824 cars.
The hardtop remained the most popular choice, and this wasn’t exactly surprising, considering it was also the most affordable version in the entire lineup. A six-cylinder-powered Mustang hardtop started at $2,618, while the newly introduced Mach 1 fastback carried a starting price tag of $3,122.
Photo: eBay seller david159043 The Mustang lineup included a plethora of engine choices for the 1969 model year, but the top choice was the Boss 429 Cobra Jet HO. It was a ridiculously expensive engine, as whoever wanted this engine had to pay no more, no less than $1,208 more on top of the Mustang price.
This Mustang Mach 1 isn’t fitted with this fantastic engine - and this isn’t a surprise because not many of these were built, so if you come across a genuine specimen, buy it without blinking because you could miss it - but it’s not a six-powered Mustang.
The Mach 1 could not be ordered with a six, but considering this is a project that’s been sitting for a long time - 30 years, according to the owner - discovering another engine under the hood wouldn’t be a surprise.
The unit in charge of putting the wheels in motion on this Mustang is a 351 Windsor, but we’re not getting any other specifics. For example, my first question would be whether this 351 is the original unit, so ask your mechanic to check everything in person before you even consider making an offer.
The engine is paired with an automatic transmission, but it’s obviously impossible to tell if they work. Considering this car has been sitting for some three decades - and by the looks of things, this happened under the clear sky, in the owner’s yard - I wouldn’t expect any good news.
Photo: eBay seller david159043 Otherwise, it’s pretty clear that this Mustang Mach 1 needs the obvious and sort of typical classic car work. It’s a project that suffers from unsurprising rust problems, though I would still go there in person to see everything live.
The Mach 1 landed online without too many specifics, so you should just ask for a walkaround video to obtain more information about this Mach 1. Nothing beats a live verification, but if you don’t want to leave on a long trip, a video that reveals more data would also come in handy.
It’s also unclear if anything big is missing, and this is critical information for anyone who wants to buy a Mach 1 for restoration. Bringing this car back to day-one specifications would be a challenge if too many parts are unavailable.
Photo: eBay seller david159043 The owner wants $12,000 for this Mach 1, but they also enabled the Make Offer option. This should be good news for potential buyers, as it’s a sign that the seller would also consider other offers, so you might be able to get a better deal if you’re committed to a purchase.
The eBay summary indicates a mileage of 35,000 miles, but it’s unclear if this is original to the car. A clean title is also available.
The vehicle is parked in Chicago, Illinois, and transportation will obviously be necessary, considering its shape. It’s also unclear if the wheels roll freely, but getting this car on your trailer shouldn’t be such a big deal with the right tools. The listing will go offline in 29 days, meaning that you have almost one month to call the seller, convince your significant other, and then go there in person to see this Mach 1 live.

PACCAR will put a factory-installed touchscreen and fleet app platform called PACCAR Connect in Kenworth and Peterbilt Class 8 trucks beginning in early 2027. The company announced the system Monday at the American Trucking Associations ’ Management Conference & Exhibition in Charlotte, North Carolina.
PACCAR said the system, which is covered under factory warranty, can eliminate the need for multiple aftermarket devices in the cab. It also connects Kenworth and Peterbilt customers to the Virtual Vehicle app marketplace from Platform Science. PACCAR made a minority equity investment in the connected-truck company in March 2023.
Connected services are already on PACCAR’s spending list. Chief Financial Officer Brice Poplawski named them among the company’s investment areas in July , alongside new powertrains and manufacturing expansion.
“PACCAR Connect advances our connected vehicle strategy,” John Rich, PACCAR’s chief technology officer, said in the release.
PACCAR is not the first truckmaker on Platform Science’s system. Virtual Vehicle was developed with Daimler Truck North America, Navistar, PACCAR and other manufacturers. Daimler became the first to integrate factory-installed telematics onto it in May 2020 .
What changes for fleets and drivers
Kenworth and Peterbilt have sold remote diagnostics as separate subscriptions. As of 2022, fleets managed Kenworth’s TruckTech+ and Peterbilt’s SmartLINQ through the PACCAR Solutions portal, Truck Parts & Service noted . The new PACCAR Connect Portal puts vehicle health, remote diagnostics, mileage, location, warranty status and idle time in one back-office tool. PACCAR did not say whether it replaces TruckTech+ or SmartLINQ.
Fleets activate third-party apps through the portal, which PACCAR said lets them bring their own workflows and technology directly into the truck.
Drivers get a high-definition touchscreen. Peterbilt’s is a 13-inch portrait screen, standard on Models 579, 589 and 567 with Class 8 interiors starting in the first quarter of 2027, Truck News reported . Kenworth uses a 15-inch center display. The voice assistant responds to more than 250 commands in English, Spanish and French, according to Transport Topics .
The display accepts up to eight camera inputs and can switch views automatically when the truck reverses or a turn signal comes on. It pairs two phones over Bluetooth at once and supports Apple CarPlay. Preloaded PACCAR apps for a digital operator’s manual, driver tutorials, vehicle health information and a dealer locator carry no extra subscription charge, Truck News reported.
A plan dating to 2023
When PACCAR and Platform Science announced their collaboration in January 2023, they said PACCAR would deploy Virtual Vehicle in Kenworth and Peterbilt trucks beginning in 2024 . The new release does not say how much of that deployment reached trucks before this launch.
PACCAR’s European brand, DAF, began supplying PACCAR Connect as standard on every new XB, XD, XF, XG and XG+ in April 2024, with 10 years of service included, according to DAF . The European version pairs an online fleet portal with an optional detachable tablet.
The North American release does not include pricing for the display, the portal or third-party marketplace apps, or list which aftermarket devices fleets could pull out of the cab. It also does not name Platform Science, though Transport Topics reported that the trucks’ app store links to Platform Science’s marketplace. According to Truck News, the display is not available as a retrofit for trucks already in service.
Rich said the platform would let PACCAR “continuously expand capabilities, integrate new technologies and enhance the driver experience.”
Why it matters: PACCAR Connect brings a factory-warranted cab display and Platform Science’s app marketplace to Kenworth and Peterbilt trucks in early 2027. Fleets still lack pricing and a list of the aftermarket devices it would replace.
